newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Former Yeltsin advisor arrested in Poland -Tass.
newsitem.headline: Former Yeltsin advisor arrested in Poland -Tass.

text.p: A former advisor to President Boris Yeltsin has been arrested in Warsaw after a joint operation by Russian and Polish police, Itar-Tass news agency said on Sunday.

Sergei Stankevich, who is also a former deputy mayor of Moscow and a former deputy in the State Duma lower house of parliament, will be detained for 30 days while a Polish court decides whether to deport him to Russia to face bribery charges, Tass said.
Russia's commercial NTV television said Stankevich had tried to disguise himself by growing a beard and having his hair cut.
Stankevich went into hiding last year after the Moscow prosecutor ordered his arrest on charges of taking bribes several years earlier.
Stankevich, a Ukrainian by birth, was known as a liberal advocate of minorities' civil rights.
Yeltsin has recently vowed to crack down on official corruption, which he believes is undermining his economic reforms.
